reason: The authorization guard relies solely on client-side localStorage for role verification (line 4-5 in admin.guard.ts). This is a broken authorization vulnerability because localStorage can be arbitrarily modified by the user via browser dev tools or XSS, allowing any user to bypass the admin check by setting localStorage.setItem('role', 'admin'). No server-side validation or secure token verification exists in the shown code.

The service reads the user's role from localStorage (line 9), which is fully user-controllable, and sends it to the backend when requesting a refund (line 10). If the backend trusts this client-supplied role for authorization decisions, a user can escalate privileges by modifying localStorage. No validation, server-side derivation, or authentication-token-based control exists in this code to prevent exploitation.

No signature verification, expiration check, or issuer validation exists in the provided code.

When the first user (e.g., an admin) hits the guard, their role is cached globally. Subsequent users (including non-admins) will then bypass the authorization check because the guard returns the cached admin role without re-fetching per-user identity. There is no per-request or per-user isolation; the HTTP call uses the current user's credentials but the result is stored in a global variable.
